newsitem.title: THAILAND: Sri Dhana says it profitable, stable.
newsitem.headline: Sri Dhana says it profitable, stable.

text.p: Thai finance and securities company Sri Dhana Finance Plc said on Wednesday it had taken measures to strengthen its financial base and remained profitable and stable.

The company statement came after the central bank this week named Sri Dhana as one of 10 finance and securities companies facing liquidity problem. It ordered the companies to increase registered capital.
Sri Dhana said its board had decided in December to raise the company's registered capital to 855 million baht from 621.25 million baht by issuing 23.375 million new shares at 10 baht each.
The issue would be for 21.3 million shares in a rights issue at 10 baht per share. It would also offer 2.075 million shares in exchange for warrants.
The moves were approved by shareholders at the end of January, the company said.
These measures had been decided upon before the central bank's recommendation to increase capital, the company said.
It added that it had made more than adequate provisioning for problem debts.

"The company always reserves for doubtful and bad debts at the higher rate that was regulated by the Bank of Thailand. In 1996, even though the doubtful debts remained at 125 billion baht, the company reserved for them 250 million baht," the statement said.
A fire at a city centre office block, which destroyed Sri Dhana's new premises, had little impact on company performance and Sri Dhana was insured against the loss, the statement said.
Sri Dhana has honoured all promissory notes, never offered margin financing to retail stock market investors and made an operational profit on securities trading in 1996, the firm said.
